title: LIST falls back from search to store scan only on the first page
answers: LIST with field selector errors instead of falling back on page 2
Store scan fallback for selectable-field filters
Why doesn't pagination fall back when the index lacks a field
How List decides between search-backed and store-scan-backed listing
body:
Invariant: when search refuses a List because the index lacks a requested selectable field (resource.IsSelectableFieldNotIndexed), the caller may fall back to a plain store scan (which reads objects and filters in-process) ONLY when req.NextPageToken is empty. A later page's continue token encodes a position in the search result set that a store scan cannot resume from, so on later pages the error must be surfaced to the client instead.
Enforced in pkg/storage/unified/resource/list_with_selectors.go:searchForList (checks req.NextPageToken == "" before converting the search error into errSearchCannotAnswerList) and pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:Server.List (treats errors.Is(err, errSearchCannotAnswerList) as the fallback signal and otherwise returns the response/error as-is).
If this ordering/guard is skipped, a mid-pagination fallback would silently restart or desync the listing instead of erroring.
applies: pkg/storage/unified/resource List path when search is used for field/label selectors

search: LIST falls back from search to store scan only on first page, requiring a req.NextPageToken == "" guard in searchForList before converting IsSelectableFieldNotIndexed errors to errSearchCannotAnswerList; later pages must surface the error instead. The invariant is enforced by checking the guard in pkg/storage/unified/resource/list_with_selectors.go:searchForList and treating errSearchCannotAnswerList as fallback signal in Server.List. Applies when the search index lacks a requested field selector in LIST operations. Skipping this guard causes mid-pagination fallbacks to silently restart or desynchronize the listing instead of erroring to the client.
